subject: Mercury-3B adoptability gap & pin request for controlled rollout
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Tim Cho <tim.cho@brightlayer.com>, BrightLayer Models <models@brightlayer.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Mercury-3B adoptability gap & pin request for controlled rollout

Team —

BrightLayer shared a Mercury-3B "adapt" variant for our partner pilot (S3 link below). Product would like to ship a controlled, regional rollout week of May 18, but we have three outstanding asks before we greenlight:

1) Compatibility checklist: confirm tokenizer parity, kv-cache behavior, and streaming/partial-responses compatibility with our serving runtime.
2) Quantization profile: recommended 8-bit / 4-bit profile and any accuracy regressions observed on our eval suite.
3) Pin request: we need a temporary version pin (no auto-upgrade) for the first 4 weeks of rollout and an ops fallback policy if latency or cost spikes.

Can you triage what we can complete by EOD May 14? I attached the variant spec and preliminary benchmarks BrightLayer provided.

S3 artifact: https://s3.redwood-inference.internal/brightlayer/mercury-3b/artifacts/
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/ACME-1874

Thanks —
Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz | Product Partnerships, Redwood Inference
From: Tim Cho <tim.cho@brightlayer.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: BrightLayer Models <models@brightlayer.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mercury-3B adoptability gap & pin request for controlled rollout

Vanessa — thanks for the clear list. We uploaded the v1 artifacts (model weights, tokenizer, quantization matrix) to the S3 path you cited this morning. Quick notes:

- Tokenizer: a small change to whitespace handling compared to Mercury-2 — we included a tokenizer-migration.md.
- KV cache: identical architecture; latency variance expected only for past-key-value encoding variant.
- We are happy to support a 4-week pin. BrightLayer recommends 8-bit quant profile for CPU fallback; 4-bit on supported GPUs.

If it helps, I can do a short demo of the model behavior at 11am PT today.

—Tim
Tim Cho | Head of Integrations, BrightLayer
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Tim Cho <tim.cho@brightlayer.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mercury-3B adoptability gap & pin request for controlled rollout

Thanks Tim/Vanessa — I pulled the artifacts. Immediate asks from runtime side:

- Please confirm exact tokenizer version file name (tokenizer.json vs tokenizer-v2.json). The migration doc references both; we need the canonical file for our ingestion pipeline.
- We will run the compatibility tests (tokenization parity, kv-cache replica test, streaming smoke tests) on a staging node. ETA: complete by 2027-05-14 18:00 PT if we get canonical artifacts and a short test harness from BrightLayer.
- On pinning: to request a temporary pin we need a JIRA with the rollout window + rollback playbook. I can draft the ticket once Priyom confirms the rollout policy.

Dev
Dev Patel | Runtime Engineering, Redwood Inference
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Tim Cho <tim.cho@brightlayer.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mercury-3B adoptability gap & pin request for controlled rollout

Couple of product/ops notes from my side:

- Rollout policy proposal: staged regional rollout (US-west -> US-east -> EU) with traffic ramp 10%/40%/100% over 72 hours and auto-fallback to Mercury-2 if token-level latency P95 exceeds 450ms or error-rate > 2%.
- For the pin: propose a 4-week pin on the variant with a canary that is allowed to auto-upgrade only after sign-off from product + runtime. Priyom will file the pin request form and the rollback playbook today.
- Priyom: can you own telemetry gating? I want a small prompt-set sanity check every 6 hours for first 72 hours.

I'll summarize and create the JIRA and a short runbook.

—Priyom
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: Tim Cho <tim.cho@brightlayer.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 15:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mercury-3B adoptability gap & pin request for controlled rollout

Quick research check-in:

- Tokenizer differences matter for our eval prompts; the tokenizer-migration.md highlights a small merge rule that lengthens some user prompts by 1–2 tokens. That could shift cost and cache-hit patterns. We need an explicit tokenization parity test and a mapped conversion table so stored prompt hashes remain interpretable.
- Eval results: the preliminary bench shows a small BLEU-ish style degradation on long-context summarization in the 4-bit profile (approx -1.8% on our regression suite). I will run the full eval matrix by EOD May 14 and add a note on where the degradation is concentrated.
- Suggested fallback behavior: if quality regression exceeds our threshold (3% on customer-critical evals) we should auto-fallback to Mercury-2 and trigger a rollback incident.

Marissa
Marissa Cole | Applied ML Research, Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Tim Cho <tim.cho@brightlayer.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mercury-3B adoptability gap & pin request for controlled rollout

Security/Compliance items to close before pin approval:

1) Artifact signing: confirm model artifacts are signed and checksums are provided (we need reproducible hashes for supply-chain audit).
2) Telemetry: define retention of model interaction logs for the pilot (30 days default); if BrightLayer requires longer retention we need a data processing agreement.
3) Encryption: confirm KMS envelope encryption of artifacts at rest in BrightLayer S3 and that keys are accessible via our Vault bridge for private deployment cases.

Rishi — can you review the fallback policy from an incident response perspective and confirm the on-call rollback steps are feasible?

Once the artifact signing + retention answers are in, I can sign off on the temporary pin with a conditional note on telemetry retention and audit logging.

Neha Kapoor | Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
